messages:
sara_ops: Heads up — Dedicated Capacity console shows 0 GPUs for cluster `horizon-prod` after last night's EKS rolling upgrade. Customer ticket #8765 reporting failed allocations and 502s. Anyone oncall? :eyes:
ben_sre: Which panel exactly? Dedicated > Pools > horizon-prod? Any screenshots or API responses?
sara_ops: Yep, Pools page. Screenshot attached in ticket but here's what the API returned when I hit the internal pool endpoint: `curl -sS https://inventory.internal/pools/horizon-prod/nodes | jq .count` -> `0`. We definitely had 12 GPU nodes before the upgrade.
mike_platform: I saw the EKS upgrade rolled a minor kubelet version bump and we changed a node label as part of a config refactor — `node.kubernetes.io/gpu=true` -> `gpu.accelerator=true`. Inventory parser expects `node.kubernetes.io/gpu` currently. Could be a label mismatch.
esther_support: Customer is escalating because Dedicated API returns "insufficient capacity" despite nodes being healthy in the cluster. Billing team flagged possible overcharge if allocation retries continued. Need fast root cause and mitigation.
lucy_devx: Quick repro steps I used in a test cluster: `kubectl get nodes -L node.kubernetes.io/gpu,gpu.accelerator -o wide` shows the new label present and old label absent on the new nodes. Inventory service list uses `labelSelector=node.kubernetes.io/gpu=true` in the k8s client.
ben_sre: Can someone paste the inventory service logs for the sync that ran at 02:10 UTC? ops-bot, do we have the deploy log?
ops-bot: deploy/inventory-service@prod rolled from tag v2.4.1 -> v2.5.0 at 02:05 UTC (CI: https://ci.internal/1234)
mike_platform: I pulled logs:
```
2026-03-17T02:10:12Z ERROR inventory.sync Failed to list nodes: permission denied (clusters: horizon-prod)
2026-03-17T02:10:13Z WARN inventory.parse No nodes matched label selector 'node.kubernetes.io/gpu=true'
2026-03-17T02:10:13Z INFO inventory.sync Completed sync: 0 nodes discovered
```
ben_sre: Two issues: 1) permission denied for the list attempt (RBAC) and 2) label mismatch. If RBAC prevented listing, parser never got to check labels — but we still shouldn't drop nodes to 0 if we can fallback to known node cache.
jordan_sre: I can confirm the inventory service's SA lost `list` permission due to a ClusterRole change during the upgrade. The upgrade applied a new managed ClusterRole which didn't include `nodes` `list` for that SA. I'll push a quick RBAC patch.
esther_support: Meanwhile customer wants a hotfix. Any way to reconcile counts so UI doesn't show 0?
mike_platform: We can force a full re-sync from cached K8s state once RBAC fixed. Command on infra-runner: `inventoryctl sync --cluster horizon-prod --force-cache-merge` — this will merge previous cached nodes with what's reachable. Will need RBAC fix first so the service can validate.
ben_sre: Also adding a fallback to accept alternate GPU label keys would prevent this class of breakage going forward — patch in tracker: INF-4921.
sara_ops: I'm running the RBAC patch now (granting `get,list,watch` for nodes to the inventory SA). Patching...
ops-bot: k8s:rolebinding/inventory-sa-binding applied to horizon-prod (rollout id: 21233)
sara_ops: RBAC landed. Starting forced sync: `inventoryctl sync --cluster horizon-prod --force`
ops-bot: inventory sync job started (job id: 8890)
mike_platform: Log tail after sync start:
```
2026-03-17T02:22:01Z INFO inventory.sync Listing nodes: 12 found
2026-03-17T02:22:02Z INFO inventory.parse Found nodes with labels: ["gpu.accelerator=true"]
2026-03-17T02:22:03Z INFO inventory.store Merged 12 nodes into pool horizon-prod
2026-03-17T02:22:04Z INFO dashboard.notify Cache invalidation event sent for pool horizon-prod
```
ben_sre: Dashboard cache invalidated, UI should reflect new counts in ~30s.
jordan_sre: Confirmed — Pools page now shows 12 GPUs. Customer notified.
esther_support: Customer updated. They're still seeing occasional 502s to the Dedicated API during the window; might be leftover request retries. Any logs?
mike_platform: The 502s were from the allocator service which hit an empty capacity set while inventory was 0. Those requests were retried and succeeded once inventory returned. We'll add circuit-breaker and short-lived fallback to cached responses to avoid 5xxs during transient inventory failures. Filed INF-4922.
lucy_devx: Action items: 1) add label fallback parsing (INF-4921) 2) strengthen RBAC preflight in rollout (INF-4923) 3) add dashboard graceful degradation to show last-known count instead of 0 for <=5m (INF-4922) 4) notify billing about transient allocation retries (esther).
sara_ops: Thanks all. I'll follow up with a postmortem and link to ticket #8765. :thumbsup:
